record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: What is the reverse-mathematical strength of statement (D), namely that for every k at least 2 the Rado graph has the rainbow Ramsey property for k-bounded colorings?

evidence.quote: (D) The Rado graph has the rainbow Ramsey property, for k-bounded colorings, for each k >= 2.
(9) What is the Reverse Mathematics strength of the statement (D)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R = (V, E) denote the Rado graph, i.e., the unique (up to isomorphism) countably infinite graph that is universal and ultrahomogeneous for finite graphs. For a finite structure A, let Age(R) denote the class of finite graphs, and for A in Age(R) let Hom(A, R) denote the set of induced copies of A inside R.

For an integer k ≥ 2, a coloring c : Hom(A, R) → ω is called k-bounded if for every color i ∈ ω, |c^{-1}(i)| ≤ k. A subset S ⊆ V is a rainbow for c if S induces a copy of R in which c is injective on the set of induced copies of A inside S.

Statement (D) is the following: for every finite graph A and every integer k ≥ 2, every k-bounded coloring c : Hom(A, R) → ω admits an induced subcopy R' ⊆ R isomorphic to R such that c restricted to Hom(A, R') is injective (i.e., R' is a rainbow for c).

Determine the precise reverse-mathematical strength of statement (D). That is, identify a subsystem of second-order arithmetic (such as RCA₀, WKL₀, ACA₀, ACA₀′, ATR₀, etc.) over which statement (D) is provably equivalent to a well-known principle, and prove the equivalence.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as an explicitly posed open question in a list of problems concerning the reverse mathematics of Ramsey-type theorems on the Rado graph. While related work establishes that the Rado graph is rainbow Ramsey for k-bounded colorings (in ZFC) and analyzes the reverse-mathematical strength of the Rainbow Ramsey Theorem for pairs on ω, no published result determining the reverse-mathematical strength of statement (D) for the Rado graph was located.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow Ramsey Simple Structures
status_evidence.snippet: Certain ultrahomogeneous binary relational structures, e.g., the Rado graph, are rainbow Ramsey.
status_evidence.claim: The Rado graph is known (in ZFC) to be rainbow Ramsey for k-bounded colorings, motivating the question of its reverse-mathematical strength.

status_evidence.title: The Strength of the Rainbow Ramsey Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: The Rainbow Ramsey Theorem for pairs is strictly weaker than Ramsey's Theorem for pairs over RCA0.
status_evidence.claim: Reverse-mathematical analyses exist for rainbow Ramsey on ω but not specifically for the Rado-graph version (D).

status_evidence.title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems including the reverse mathematics strength of statement (D).
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in a problem list.
